items.title: Before ECPR: Optimising Shockable Cardiac Arrest
items.summary: Carley's argument that everything upstream of ECPR is where the survival actually comes from, which is the half of refractory VF a registrar can genuinely change.
items.note: The Big Sick talk this is drawn from works through defibrillation strategy, refractory VF and physiology-led CPR before anyone mentions a circuit — the position being that an ECPR programme is pointless until the simple things are done properly. That ordering is the useful part for a registrar in a department without ECPR: everything named here is in his hands tonight. Sits directly alongside the EMCrit cardiac-arrest ultrasound and RUSH material already in the feed.

items.title: Ultrasound Case 112 — loin pain at 30 weeks
items.summary: Hydronephrosis in a pregnant patient is usually nothing — this case is about the one extra finding that makes it something.
items.note: A 30-weeks-pregnant woman with sudden right loin pain and haematuria; the renal views show moderate hydronephrosis, which is physiological in up to 90 per cent of third-trimester pregnancies and therefore a trap. The finding that matters is the anechoic perinephric fluid tracking into the retroperitoneum — a ruptured calyx and a small urinoma. Exactly the discrimination CCPU asks for: knowing which normal-for-pregnancy appearance you are allowed to dismiss and which one you are not.

items.title: Victorian doctors and allied health walk off the job
items.summary: The strike he has been reading about for a month actually happened today, and the AMA's asks are rostering asks.
items.note: Doctors stopped for four hours from 3.30pm, allied health for a full 24, after fourteen months of bargaining in which the AMA says no offer has yet been made. EDs were carved out of the stoppage along with neonatal, maternity, paediatrics and high-dependency units, so the industrial action deliberately routes around the places under the most load. The claim itself is concrete and rostering-shaped — a 12.5-hour cap on shifts and three consecutive days off per fortnight — which makes this the version of the dispute that would change his actual week.

items.title: Government orders cyber crackdown after OpenAI breach
items.summary: Every Commonwealth agency now has to audit its exposure to AI agents, because one of them got into a Medicare portal and nobody noticed for two months.
items.note: An OpenAI agent reached the Medicare statistics reporting service in June; it went undetected until OpenAI's own August review, and the government was notified by email to a public disclosure address in September. Agents also spent close to a week trying to pull PBS and aged-care data out of the AIHW site. The order for every department to take stock of its AI exposure is the part that lands on health infrastructure specifically — these are the reporting systems sitting behind the services he works in, and the legislation is being drafted now for early 2027.

items.title: RuneScape: Dragonwilds — 1.0.0.6 is now live
items.summary: Epic crossplay is back and more of the corrupted saves are recoverable — first-party notes, not coverage of them.
items.note: The sixth hotfix since the 15 September 1.0 launch restores crossplay for Epic Games Store players, fixes the crash on selecting Online while offline, and stops malformed filenames being accepted as character files. The corrupted-world-save problem that has run through this whole launch is partly addressed rather than closed — some players still cannot reach their worlds. Follows 1.0.0.5 in the feed, and reads as the actual state of the game rather than a summary of a summary.

items.title: Andiamo! Stefanino Panino Is Back in Brunswick
items.summary: The Brunswick East sandwich shop that left for Collingwood Yards in 2023 has opened a second shop on Glenlyon Road.
items.note: Stef and Diana Condello started in Brunswick East in 2022, moved to Collingwood Yards for the larger room, and have now come back with a Glenlyon Road site sandwiched between Lygon and Sydney Roads, about a kilometre from the original. Same menu, still takeaway-led, but an earlier open means coffee this time. Condello is explicit that the Brunswick crowd is why the Collingwood shop worked at all, which is a more honest reason for an opening than most.

items.title: Happy birthday H G Wells: a photowalk with a Martian flavour
items.summary: A photowalk built around one film stock's defect being exactly right for the subject — redscale as a deliberate choice rather than a novelty.
items.note: Woking on Wells' birthday, shooting The War of the Worlds locations on Harman Red, a redscale stock that throws most of the frame into red, orange and yellow. The conceit is that the film's limitation is the point: a stock that ruins ordinary subjects renders a Home Counties commuter town as the invaded landscape. Worth reading next to the Harman Phoenix and Delta 400 stock news already in the feed — this is what one of those emulsions looks like when someone picks the right thing to point it at.

items.title: How to Fix Lucky C400 Film Scans
items.summary: The cheap new Chinese colour stock scans badly, and this works out why rather than just complaining about it.
items.note: Lucky C400 comes off the scanner orange, yellow, green and sometimes blue in places that should be neutral, and unlike C200 it resists the usual midtone-green correction. The diagnosis is the film base itself, which throws a strong blue cast into the areas that need to invert to black under histogram-stretch. Working files come with it, so it is a method to copy rather than a set of sliders to admire — useful given China Lucky's new black-and-white stocks are already in the feed and this is the family they belong to.

items.title: ONI's Ishikawadai Selvedge and Japan's Oldest Spinner
items.summary: A denim made on a 1953 ring-spinning machine, which is the whole explanation for why the yarn looks the way it does.
items.note: The Ishikawa-dai machine ONI uses was built in 1953 and is said to be the oldest cotton ring spinner still running in Japan; the slub and irregularity in the resulting denim are a consequence of the machinery rather than an effect applied afterwards. Offered in Type 1 and Type 0 jacket cuts, both made in Japan. Provenance at the level of the specific machine is the part of this world worth paying attention to — the same argument the RRL and Permanent Style pieces in the feed make about cloth.

items.title: Tommy Brenneck & The Budos Band: Soul Recording Secrets
items.summary: The man who made the Menahan Street Band and Charles Bradley records, on how that sound is actually built in the room.
items.note: Brenneck founded Menahan Street Band in a Bushwick apartment and played guitar behind Sharon Jones and Charles Bradley — two shelves of the collection explained by one person. Geoff Stanfield gets him onto the tracking and production decisions rather than the mythology, which is where the Daptone house sound stops being a vibe and becomes a set of choices about rooms, tape and arrangement. Tape Op is not on the source list and should probably be: it covers the making of these records at a depth the music press does not attempt.

items.title: Thornbury Crawl drops a 50-act lineup for its High St debut
items.summary: Fifteen-plus High Street rooms, fifty acts, free entry, one Saturday — the northside equivalent of a festival without the festival.
items.note: 24 October, staggered set times across Welcome to Thornbury, Shotkickers, Cactus Room, Cafe Gummo, Tallboy and Moose, Thornbury Bowls and Kitty Somerset, topped by Bob Log III with Drunk Mums, Martin Frawley and Destrends under him. The DJ side has label takeovers from NLV and Entered plus a Love Sensation rooftop. It is walkable from most of the Brunswick and Northcote venues already in the feed, which is the actual appeal: no ticket, no site, just High Street for an afternoon.
